channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Expedite Talks with Foreign Airlines on Fifth Freedom Rights
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to accelerate negotiations with foreign airlines regarding "fifth freedom" traffic rights. President Mirziyoyev emphasized expanding international air travel, noting interest from airlines like Turkish Airlines and Etihad. The country aims to facilitate easier access for travelers from regions currently requiring transit.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ranks in UN Top 20 for E-Government Development, Improving Digital Access
item.description: Kazakhstan has entered the UN's top 20 for e-government development, moving from 24th to 16th place. The country also significantly improved its mobile connectivity and internet access ranking, climbing 28 spots to 13th. "Kazakhtelecom" is expanding fiber-optic internet to rural areas, aiming to connect 3,008 villages by 2027.

item.title: Underground Call Center in Tashkent Defrauded European Citizens Using Crypto Assets
item.description: Law enforcement in Tashkent has shut down an underground call center that defrauded European citizens. Ten individuals allegedly contacted Europeans via messengers, offering fake document services and trading courses. They used deceptive schemes to steal funds, converting them to cryptocurrency. Authorities seized equipment and are investigating crypto asset trafficking.

item.title: Four Convicted in Almaty for Fictitious Employment Scheme, State Losses Recovered
item.description: Four individuals have been convicted in Almaty for their involvement in a fictitious employment scheme that caused six million tenge in damages to the state. Two officials from the "Career Center of Almaty City" organized illegal salary payments for individuals who did not perform actual work. The state's losses have been fully compensated.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Teenager Convicted for Murdering and Burning Boyfriend's Body
item.description: A 15-year-old girl in Kazakhstan's Turkistan region has been convicted of murdering her boyfriend and burning his body. The incident occurred in May when the victim's body was found near an old factory. The girl, who had recently finished ninth grade, reportedly stabbed the 20-year-old multiple times after he refused to end their relationship.

item.title: Pavlodar Oncology Center Opens New Radiotherapy Unit with Advanced Linear Accelerator
item.description: The Pavlodar Regional Oncology Center has launched a new radiotherapy unit featuring a state-of-the-art linear accelerator and a CT simulator. The project, costing 3.2 billion tenge, aims to improve cancer treatment precision and reduce side effects. This upgrade aligns with national healthcare modernization goals.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Tajikistan Premiere Joint Film on Jami and Navoi in Dushanbe
item.description: A historical drama, 'The Radiance of Stars: Jami and Navoi,' a joint production by Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, premiered in Dushanbe. The film explores the lives and works of poets Abdurahmon Jami and Alisher Navoi. "Tajikfilm" director Mahmadsaid Shokhiyon highlighted the project's cultural significance. The 144-minute film, in Tajik and Uzbek, covers 1469-1492.

item.title: UN Report: Young People Face Growing Challenges in Starting Adult Life
item.description: A UN Population Fund report indicates that while today's youth are more educated, achieving financial independence, homeownership, and starting families is increasingly difficult. Economic instability, high housing costs, and conflicts hinder life plans. One in five young people globally are disengaged from education or employment, with AI posing further uncertainty.

item.title: 990 Trucks Stuck at Uzbekistan-Kazakhstan Border, Causing 40km Queue
item.description: A 40-kilometer queue of 990 trucks has formed at the B. Konysbayev border crossing between Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan. Drivers report waiting for several days to cross. The congestion is attributed to increased cargo flow from China via Kazakhstan and transit from Russia and Belarus. Uzbekistan is negotiating a 'One Stop' customs system with Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Malaysia to Resettle 10,000 Rohingya Refugees in Turkey Through Skills Training
item.description: Malaysia announced a program to resettle 10,000 Rohingya refugees currently in Malaysia to Turkey, providing them with skills training. This initiative, supported by Turkey, aims to offer a more coordinated and humane solution to the Rohingya situation.

item.title: Kazakh President Assigns Tasks to New National Security Committee Chairman
item.description: The President of Kazakhstan has given instructions to the newly appointed Chairman of the National Security Committee. The specific tasks and details of the instructions were not disclosed in the report.

item.title: China Purchases Monkeys for Experiments Amidst Global Competition
item.description: China has begun purchasing monkeys for its laboratory experiments, acquiring over 30,000 primates from Cambodia. This move intensifies a global race for research animals, following a previous US-Cambodia partnership that was halted due to a smuggling dispute. A new competition between the US and China is anticipated.

item.title: Thirty Families in Atyrau Receive Keys to New Apartments
item.description: Thirty families in Atyrau have received keys to new rental apartments with the right to purchase. The keys were presented by the regional governor and the chairman of "Otbasy Bank." The bank has programs supporting youth, medical workers, and rural residents, with 689 individuals housed since 2022.

item.title: Taliban Leader Describes Ghazni as Land of Saints and Martyrs
item.description: Taliban leader Hibatullah Akhundzada visited Ghazni province, calling it the 'cultural capital of Islam, land of saints, scholars, martyrs, and city of knowledge.' He emphasized obedience, administrative improvement, spreading knowledge, justice, and strengthening security. He also urged the reformation of youth through authentic Islamic and Afghan culture.

item.title: Tokayev Meets New National Security Chief, Gives Specific Instructions
item.description: President Tokayev met with the new Chairman of the National Security Committee, Marat Irmenov, to hear reports on ongoing national security work and future tasks. The meeting focused on reforming and increasing the efficiency of national security agencies. Tokayev also gave specific instructions regarding corruption prevention.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Tax Service Reports Top 5 Reforms in Five Years
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's tax revenues have nearly tripled in five years, reaching 308 billion soms in 2025 and exceeding 338 billion through October 2026. The State Tax Service highlighted five key reforms, including digitalization of services, new control methods, business support, and expanded benefits. Over 1.7 million users now utilize electronic tax services.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Meets with National Security Committee Chairman
item.description: The President of Kazakhstan received Marat Irmenov, Chairman of the National Security Committee, to hear a report on ongoing work to ensure national security and future objectives. Measures for reforming and increasing the efficiency of national security agencies were presented. The President issued specific instructions at the meeting's conclusion.

item.title: Elon Musk Accuses Zelensky of Lying About Starlink Usage
item.description: Elon Musk accused Ukrainian President Zelensky of lying about Starlink, after Zelensky complained that reduced satellite internet speed made it difficult to shoot down Russian drones. The SpaceX chief stated that Kyiv was abusing the network. This follows reports of Starlink's effectiveness in Ukraine.

item.title: Kazakh President Hears Report on National Security Committee Reform
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev received a report from the Chairman of the National Security Committee (KNB), Marat Ermenov, regarding reforms within the security agency. The report detailed measures to enhance national security and future tasks. The President issued further instructions following the meeting.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Use $2.2 Billion in Materials for Jizzakh Nuclear Power Plant Construction
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to utilize $2.2 billion worth of materials for the construction of the Jizzakh nuclear power plant. A special industrial zone will be established to produce 70 types of required products. The president also emphasized improving local construction materials and analyzing demand for import-substituting materials.

item.title: New Head of National Security Committee Reports to President on Agency Reform
item.description: The new Chairman of the National Security Committee (KNB), Marat Irmenov, reported to President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev on national security measures and future tasks. Tokayev was informed about ongoing reforms to enhance the KNB's effectiveness. The President issued several directives following the meeting.

item.title: Taliban Forces Panjshir Residents to Give Interviews, Repeat Pre-Written Statements
item.description: Local sources in Panjshir report that the Taliban are forcing residents to give interviews to Taliban-controlled media, repeating specific sentences provided by the authorities. These interviews are allegedly conducted under threat of torture and imprisonment by Taliban intelligence forces.

item.title: Kazakh Minister of Culture Meets Azerbaijan's Ambassador to Discuss Cooperation
item.description: Arman Kyryqbayev, Kazakhstan's Minister of Culture and Information, met with Azerbaijan's Ambassador Alimirzamin Askerov to discuss developing cooperation in culture, museums, media, and creative industries. They reviewed the preparation of a cultural cooperation program for 2026-2028, aligned with agreements from President Ilham Aliyev's visit.

item.title: New Building for Bishkek Music College to Be Completed by Year-End
item.description: The new building for the Murataly Kurenkeyev Kyrgyz National Music College in Bishkek is scheduled for completion by the end of the year. The facility will offer modern conditions for individual practice, rehearsals, and a concert hall for 370 people. This new eight-story complex will replace the older, smaller building, despite some student opposition to the demolition.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Allocate 5,000 Hectares for Tourism Projects
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to allocate an additional 5,000 hectares of land for tourism development, building on the 1,200 hectares already reserved. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev emphasized the need to develop infrastructure and service sectors to ensure year-round tourism. The country is preparing for its first international tourism investment forum in Tashkent, expecting over 100 investors.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Exempting Problem Loan Write-offs from Personal Income Tax
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering exempting individuals from personal income tax (PIT) when problem loan debts are forgiven, within set limits. The government also proposed reducing write-off limits for banks and microfinance organizations. A second amendment aims to provide tax incentives for domestic light industry producers.

item.title: Russia and Uzbekistan Sign Military Cooperation Plan for 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan and Russia have signed a military cooperation plan for 2027, following talks between Russian Defense Minister Andrei Belousov and his Uzbek counterpart, Botiir Kudratkhodjaev. The plan aims to strengthen security in Central Asia. The two countries are also implementing a broader military strategic partnership program for 2026-2030.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Tax Exemption for Written-Off Loans and Microloans
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering a proposal to exempt individuals from personal income tax (PIT) on written-off problematic debts from loans and microloans. The amendment was approved by the Project Office for Tax Code Implementation. The proposal aims to simplify debt forgiveness for borrowers without additional requirements, within creditor limits.

item.title: Turkish Company Betek to Build Paint Factory Near Tashkent for $30 Million
item.description: Turkish company Betek will construct a paint and varnish factory in the Zangiata district, near Tashkent, with an investment of $30 million. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev instructed local authorities to study consumer demand and international brand capabilities to propose projects reducing finished product imports, which currently amount to $280 million annually.

item.title: Kazakhstan Suspends Microfinance Organization License Due to Repeated Violations
item.description: The license of 'Beineu Credit Partnership' LLC for microfinance activities in Kazakhstan has been suspended. The Financial Market Development Agency cited repeated failures to submit reports to the National Bank and violations of laws and regulations as reasons for the suspension. This prohibits new microcredit agreements and changes to existing ones.

item.title: Almaty Named Among World's Top 20 Tourist Destinations for 2027 by BBC Travel
item.description: Almaty has been included in BBC Travel's list of recommended destinations for 2027, alongside countries like Japan and France. The publication highlighted Almaty's developing culinary and artistic scene, its scenic location near the Tian Shan mountains, and potential new direct flights to New York, Abu Dhabi, and Hong Kong.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Dismisses Head of Transport Development Department
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed the head of the department for the development of the transport sector. The reason for the dismissal was not specified in the announcement.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Orders Review of All Railway and Domestic Flight Schedules
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has instructed officials to review and revise all railway and domestic flight schedules within one month. The directive also emphasizes activating negotiations with foreign airlines to utilize the "fifth freedom of the air" regime.

item.title: CIS Interparliamentary Assembly Agrees on 35th Anniversary Program and 2027 Work Plan
item.description: The Interparliamentary Assembly (IPA) of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) held meetings in Turkmenistan's Avaza tourist zone. Discussions focused on strengthening inter-parliamentary cooperation and future priorities. Valentina Matviyenko was re-elected Chair of the IPA Council. Turkmenistan's Mejlis received observer status.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Builds Social Facilities: Hospice, Schools, and Kindergarten Under Construction
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is constructing four social facilities: a 70-bed hospice for parents of children with cancer, two schools for 975 students, and a 75-place kindergarten. The projects are funded by the President's Stabilization Fund and are proceeding on schedule, with construction progressing as planned.

item.title: Panama's Environment Minister Accuses World of Stockholm Syndrome Towards 'Oil Mafia'
item.description: At the UN COP31 climate summit, Panama's Environment Minister Juan Carlos Navarro criticized the fossil fuel industry, accusing the world of having Stockholm Syndrome towards the 'oil mafia.' He urged for a change in decision-making processes regarding climate policy and fossil fuel phase-out.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Russia Defense Ministers Discuss Military Cooperation in Khiva
item.description: The Defense Ministers of Uzbekistan and Russia held official talks in Khiva, Uzbekistan. Discussions focused on the current state, achievements, and future priorities of military cooperation between the two nations. Ministers signed documents aimed at expanding cooperation and strengthening mutual ties.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Discusses Further Cooperation with World Bank and ADB
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers met with representatives from the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to discuss future cooperation. The discussions focused on supporting the country's socio-economic development priorities, with officials highlighting recent high GDP growth and increased investment.

item.title: China Media Corporation Hosts APEC Financial Night Forum in Shenzhen
item.description: China Media Corporation organized the 'APEC Financial Night' event in Shenzhen, focusing on 'Openness, Innovation, and Cooperation.' The forum gathered Chinese and international business representatives, economists, and analysts to discuss practical economic interactions within the Asia-Pacific region.

item.title: Afghanistan Postpones Major Water Diversion from Amu Darya Until 2030
item.description: Afghanistan will delay significant water diversion from the Amu Darya River via the Kштепа Canal until at least 2030, according to Uzbekistan's Water Resources Minister. Negotiations continue between Uzbekistan and Afghanistan to agree on water volumes. The canal is not currently drawing water from the river.
